patch.value: A publish that npm accepts late is reported as failed and the GitHub Release is skipped on bun mirror lag

The daily release workflow treated a delayed npm registry propagation as a failed publish, and let bun mirror lag decide whether a GitHub Release is created at all. Three changes, applied as anchored in-place replacements by the hub's apply.py (companion item pm-cli-website-3y5d): (1) the publish reconcile window widens from 5 x 30 s to 20 x 30 s (10 minutes) with npm view --prefer-online, and the never-visible failure message now states exactly what is known instead of the false 'failed after 3 attempts', preserving the unattested-occupant refusal byte-for-byte; (2) 'Create GitHub release' no longer depends on the bun mirror - it runs whenever the publish and the tag push succeeded (step ids + outcome + !cancelled()), and a dedicated gate step fails the job visibly via 'Fail the job on bun verification failure' after a 10-minute bun window; (3) a new 'Backfill missing GitHub releases' step creates missing Releases for attested tags, using the same pm-changelog notes command scoped to the missing tag's range. Proof: stub harness 5/5 against this repo's patched release.yml, fails 4/5 on the unpatched file; grep proofs reconcile_attempts=20=1, seq 1 20=1, Backfill missing GitHub releases=1; actionlint clean.

value.author: claude-orchestrator
value.text: Greptile P1 on PR #108: the widened bun loop slept 30 s after its 20th failed attempt and then gave up without reading again, so a version installable in that last pause still failed the job. Now 21 attempts with pauses only between them (20 x 30 s, same 10-minute window), error names the real count. Proof: new harness scenario s6 (bun resolves at tick 20) fails on the previous loop (rc=1, 20 adds) and passes on this one (attempt 21 succeeds, rc=0); scenarios s1-s5 still pass; shellcheck clean.

value.author: claude-orchestrator
value.text: CodeRabbit (major) on PR #108: the backfill tag glob admitted v2026.09.18foo (whose day part breaks the 10# arithmetic and, under set -e, the step) and v2026.09.20-rc.1 (an unintended prerelease backfill), and the step could still cancel today's release despite its best-effort comment. Now: git tag -l 'v*' filtered by the anchored ^v[0-9]{4}\.[0-9]{2}\.[0-9]{2}(-[0-9]+)?$ and continue-on-error: true on the step. Proof: harness scenario s7 (tags v2026.09.20-rc.1, v2026.09.18foo, v2026.09.18-2, all npm-attested) fails on the glob (rc=1) and passes on the filter (rc=0, only v2026.09.18-2 backfilled). Harness v2 also hardens itself: HOME is the scenario dir and it aborts unless npm/npx/gh/git/bun resolve to stubs (adversarially verified: 9 aborts, 0 blocks run). 7/7 scenarios pass, 3 consecutive runs.

value.author: fleet-wave-script
value.text: Review follow-up (Greptile on pm-brief#124 and pm-linear#121): the backfill step is removed from this wave. It treated any npm attestation as proof that a tag's artifact was ours. The right check is not attested-commit equals tag-commit: this fleet's provenance records the workflow trigger commit (companion item pm-cli-website-nodo), measured as the tag's direct parent on pm-linear 2026.9.18, pm-github 2026.9.11 and pm-todos 2026.9.11. The check has to be repository plus workflow path plus ancestry, and it returns in the canonical pm-ops release verifier (companion pm-cli-website-mxrp). The other two changes, the 10-minute npm visibility window and the Release decoupled from bun lag, fix the root causes on their own. The three historical orphans were backfilled by hand on 2026-09-22.

patch.value: Final release.yml is byte-identical to a fresh run of the anchored applier on origin/main (identical), names only unbraind/pm-ts-starter, and passes the stub harness 5/5 (the unpatched file fails the four fix scenarios). Review follow-ups folded in: bun end-of-window re-check, backfill removed, max_attempts declared before use.

Companion item pm-cli-website-3y5d. Two changes to this repository's own release.yml: (1) a 10-minute npm visibility window after a reported publish error, read with --prefer-online, and an honest message when nothing becomes visible (the unattested-occupant refusal is unchanged; max_attempts is declared before the function that expands it); (2) the GitHub Release depends only on the publish and tag-push outcomes, and bun gets a 21-attempt 10-minute window with a final re-check, failing the job visibly through a separate gate step. A backfill step was proposed and removed after review: an npm attestation alone does not prove a tag's commit produced the artifact, and this fleet's provenance names the trigger commit (pm-cli-website-nodo), so provenance-ancestry verification moves to pm-cli-website-mxrp.

Final release.yml is byte-identical to a fresh run of the anchored applier on origin/main and names only unbraind/pm-ts-starter. The stub harness passes the 5 applicable scenarios on it (late-visible publish, never-visible, unattested occupant, bun failure with Release plus red job, bun resolving at the 10-minute mark), and the unpatched file fails the four fix scenarios. The backfill was removed in review.

A publish that npm accepts late is reconciled instead of reported as failed, and the GitHub Release is created whenever the publish and the tag push succeed, even when bun's mirror lags; a bun failure still fails the job visibly.

Widened the npm visibility window after a reported publish error to 10 minutes and made the GitHub Release depend only on the publish and tag-push outcomes, with bun verification failing the job visibly through a gate step. A proposed backfill step was removed after review (provenance-ancestry verification tracked as pm-cli-website-mxrp).
